note: Generated by scripts/build-skills.mjs. "backing" states what actually enforces each skill. Host activation is NOT verified; see docs/IDE_COMPATIBILITY.md.

agents.description: Orchestrates a read-only documentation audit by running the DocSutra scan, routes findings to the right specialist skill and reports verified versus unverified results. Use when asked to audit, review or health-check repository documentation.

Finds and fixes broken relative links, stale heading anchors, case-sensitive path mismatches and undefined reference links in Markdown. Use when links, anchors or file moves/renames may have broken documentation.
Checks documented shell commands against a declared CLI contract (subcommands and flags) in docsutra.config.json. Use when CLI flags, subcommands or help output changed and docs may be stale.

Detects credentials, unsafe URL schemes, pipe-to-shell installs and destructive commands in documentation, with values redacted. Use before publishing docs, open-sourcing a repo or sharing audit output.
Finds missing image alt text, empty link text, skipped heading levels and duplicate headings in Markdown docs. Use when improving documentation accessibility or WCAG alignment.
Classifies shell snippets in docs by risk (pipe-to-shell, destructive, package-install, network, mutation, inert) without running them. Use to plan which documented examples are safe to test.
Independently challenges audit findings by reproducing them from source before they are reported or patched. Use before presenting findings as fact or before applying any fix.

Compares two audit reports to show new and resolved documentation findings, and gates CI on regressions only. Use when reviewing pull requests, preparing releases or asking what changed in docs health.

Guides evidence-labelled fact-checking of documentation claims against repository source, with explicit uncertainty. Use when a doc statement about behaviour, defaults or versions must be checked against code.
Guides comparing documented API endpoints and SDK method signatures to the actual schema or source. Use when an OpenAPI spec, TypeDoc output or exported symbols changed.
Guides validating JSON/YAML examples in docs against their schema. Use when documentation shows config or payload examples that must match a schema.
Guides writing minimal, correct documentation examples grounded in real source and verified by the project test tooling. Use when a guide needs a new or repaired code example.
Guides checking that architecture diagrams and their surrounding text match real modules and services. Use when code structure changed and diagrams in docs may be outdated.
Guides comparing translated documentation to its source language for missing sections, broken links and stale content. Use when maintaining multilingual docs.
Guides producing the smallest reviewable documentation fix for verified findings, as a preview diff. Use after findings are verified and the user wants proposed edits.
Guides drafting accurate release notes and migration guidance from git history and changelog entries. Use when preparing a release or upgrade guide.
